# Findability and Accessibility of historical Raw Sunspot Numbers

The Sunspot Number (S<sub>N</sub>, formerly the International Sunspot Number) still carries scale jumps such as the 1947 “Waldmeier break”, even after two recalibrations. FARSuN responds by replaying the entire observing chain: **gather sources**, **process data** with Transkribus models and double keying, **validate and standardise** through harmonised observer IDs and calibration curves, and **disseminate** machine-readable products via APIs and VO/EPN-TAP. Legacy corpora like [Wolf’s *Mittheilungen* (1610–1918)](./mittheilungen_data-1800.qmd) are now fully integrated with automated QC monitoring NG>NS or metadata gaps, while the complete run of [Zürich observation tables (1945–1979)](./zurich_tables.qmd) has been digitised with detailed metadata finished for 1945–1959 and observer scaling analyses underway. Dense, spotless-day rich material—[C. H. Adams notebooks (1819–1823)](./adams.qmd) and [Gruithuisen manuscripts (1817–1849)](./gruithuisen.qmd)—is undergoing calibration, orientation, and dual QC before release, and the [Augustin Stark ledgers (1813–1835)](./stark.qmd) are being normalised so weather notes align with group counts. Next milestones include expanding uncertainty dashboards, citizen-science transcription workflows, exposing the consolidated database through VO services, and using the harmonised record as the foundation for S<sub>N</sub> V3 and long-term solar activity studies.
